signals.text: Plays such as Blood Brothers and The Crucible are studied in-depth at GCSE, whereas A Level students work with a panoply of plays, old and new, including Our Country’s Good and Jerusalem.

Through a dynamic curriculum that covers a wide range of topics - including app development, database design, programming, website creation, game development, cybersecurity, and hardware - students gain valuable experience in both theoretical and practical aspects of computer science.

Enrichment opportunities The Whitgift Biomedical Science Diploma, available to Lower Sixth students, offers an in-depth exploration of biomedical sciences, providing a solid foundation for those interested in pursuing careers in healthcare and research.
Field trips to Devon, designed for A Level students, offer hands-on field study experiences, where students can observe and analyse ecological systems in a natural setting.
In the Junior Years, pupils are introduced to a broad range of challenging and exciting literature, enhancing their critical thinking, writing, and communication skills.

A diverse and grounded community where every person belongs - to a circle of friends, a team, a pursuit and a shared purpose. Here, pupils are known, nurtured and challenged. Through exceptional teaching, unrivalled opportunities and deep personal support of each boy, they become more: ready to step forward with confidence into their future.
Vision, Values and Identity
Junior Years 10-13 The beginning of a Whitgiftians journey is in the Junior Years - a time where natural curiosity and independent learning are encouraged to grow and students are exposed to a wealth of new ideas, activities and learning opportunities.
Alongside equipping them for academic success, the Middle Years at Whitgift will support students to mature emotionally, helping them to develop a strong sense of who they are and what they want to accomplish.
Students in Whitgift’s Sixth Form are immersed in a challenging yet hugely rewarding experience, with inspiring tutors who support them as they prepare for their chosen path after Whitgift.
Whitgift has allowed me to pave my own way towards discovering where my true passions and interests lie, be it through academic interests, the violin or CCF. By promoting an ethos in which failure is acceptable in the pursuit of our goals, Whitgift has allowed me to find enjoyment in that process of becoming a better, more well-rounded student, as well as a better person.
WE ARE WHITGIFT
Discover our Stories
QUOTE FROM CURRENT PARENT 2026
Best Boys' Day & Boarding School 2026 - London
Whitgift is pleased to be named Best Boys' Day & Boarding School 2026 - London, recognised in the Private Education Awards.
Hybrid Sports Pitches
Whitgift is pleased to announce the completion of the School’s third hybrid pitch, located on Edridge, following the successful installations on Big Side and Puntabout in 2021.
Comprehensive Whitgift bus routes
Whitgift operates an extensive School Bus service to cater for the needs of many pupils, particularly where there are no direct public transport links.
year link with Urawa High School, Japan
Whitgift welcomed 20 students in April 2025 from Urawa High School, Japan marking over three decades of cultural exchange between the two schools.
International Partnership
Launch of a new partnership with Symbiquest Education and Riba, operator of Suchitra Academy, as part of a multi-school deal in India.
The start of the legacy
In 1596, John Whitgift, Archbishop of Canterbury (1583 to 1604) set about making his vision to educate the young people of Croydon a reality. Little did he know his founding principles would still live on in today's Whitgift.
Co-curricular activities on offer
Whitgift has a vibrant and diverse co-curricular programme ranging from Animal Club to Warhammer club.
Raised in Whitgift's Giving Day 2026
An incredible £161,157 was raised from 331 donors for the Whitgift For All Bursary Fund.
Russell Group places
In 2026, Upper Sixth Form students achieved their outstanding results through a commitment to sustained hard work and motivation from their applications to higher education and employment. 80% were awarded Russell Group places including University of St Andrew's and University of Bath.

Headmaster's Welcome
Thank you for your interest in Whitgift, a School where boys are challenged, supported, and celebrated as they learn, grow and forge lasting friendships within an astonishing educational environment.
A Whitgift education is rooted in both breadth and depth: a rich and demanding academic programme, exceptional sport, dynamic music and drama, and a multitude of inspiring, sector leading co-curricular opportunities. These extend well beyond the classroom, through trips, expeditions, and international tours that broaden horizons and foster a truly global outlook, extended yet further by our partner institution in India.
This diversity of experience is reflected in the boys themselves - a vibrant community of learners drawn from many backgrounds, grounded by their connection to Croydon and the capital beyond. Our boarders further enhance Whitgift’s global dimension; and, along with the incredible possibilities on offer, it is these impressive young men that set Whitgift apart.
Ours is a school where pupils understand the importance of character and curriculum, remaining grounded in their approach as well as achieving outstanding academic and broader success. We believe in nurturing the whole person, and that a Whitgiftian is defined not just by what he achieves, but by the relationships he builds and the integrity with which he lives. We take great pride in our commitment to service, our locality and the needs of others, and it is this very human side of Whitgift that complements our leavers’ readiness for today’s complex world.
This emphasis on our humanity is reflected our core values. Whilst here, boys develop a sense of ambition, curiosity, courage, respect and above all belonging. These underpin both our ambitious plans for the future and our decisions made in the present.
Life for all at Whitgift is full, fun, and fulfilling. Here, every boy is well known and valued; coupled with our values-centred approach, our dedicated pastoral care and attention to the individual further the sense of belonging and enable boys to find their own place and path, expertly guided by our talented and engaging staff.
To experience the spirit of Whitgift for yourself, we warmly invite you to explore this website, or better yet, visit our beautiful and distinctive campus and meet the fabulous people who make this such a remarkable community in which to learn and live. We look forward to welcoming you.

Our Vision, Values and Identity

Junior Years
Your Guide to Whitgift Life
In the Junior Years (Lower First, First and Second Form), an innovative and challenging curriculum prepares students for long-term success.
Within traditional subjects, your son will be inspired by the highest-calibre of teachers and given opportunities to encounter subjects in unique and surprising ways.
Alongside traditional subjects, your son will engage with courses preparing him for the challenges and realities of the 21st century. How can we disagree well and engage with countless different perspectives that exist across the world? What responsibilities and connections do we have for other human beings thousands of miles away? How can we navigate a world in which truth has become divisive?
Outside the classroom, through our House system and broad Co-curricular programme, he will have the opportunity to explore new interests alongside boys of different ages and backgrounds. As well as enriching his school life, and providing the opportunity to make long-lasting friendships, this will help your son develop a healthy confidence and teach him the values of respect, tolerance, and resilience. These values are central to the culture of our school community.
First Form Play Series
As a component of the Whitgift 7 programme, the ‘First Form Play Series’ began in 2023. A total of five unique 30-minute shows, all written by members of staff, are performed by the entire First Form cohort over the academic year. They are designed to introduce pupils to the world of drama and instill a passion for the subject from the start of their Whitgift journey.
Junior House System
There are 10 Houses in Junior Years, all names after trees. Lower First, First and Second Formers work together on different challenges that test all apptitudes and abilities. If you have an older sibling or parent who attended Whitgift, you will be placed in the same house as they were so keeping up traditions.
Collaboration
There is a huge benefit for all parties when older Whitgiftians support the development of those in the Junior Years. The House System achieves this well, with students from all Forms interacting on a weekly basis. In addition, regular competitions or challenges involve older Whitgiftians mentoring and offering academic support to younger students.
Physical Activity
Games and Physical Education are regular parts of the timetable, helping younger students to develop healthy attitudes to exercise. The First Form Sports Day is a hugely popular event in which each Junior House competes to win the prized cup.
Lent Collection Concert
This concert celebrates the array of musical ensembles and solos across the School and, for some First Former pupils is their first live performance for parents, which we hope will inspire them to continue on their musical journey.
Design Technology and Engineering
Whitgift has some excellent facilities and the DTE Department allows students to handle a number of tasks and projects, so you can expect to have many interesting new artifacts sent home!

Middle Years
Your Guide to School Life
Your son’s Middle Years (Third, Fourth and Fifth Form) will equip him for success in his GCSEs whilst also ensuring he develops a strong sense of who he is and what he wants to accomplish in the future.
Throughout these crucial years, he will be inspired, stretched, and supported, developing the trusting relationships and effective routines that will help him achieve more than he believed he could.
His school life will become richer, as he begins to experience a type of learning only possible outside the classroom. The learning facilities he will use, and how he uses them, will mature. He will talk to Sixth Form students about their chosen subjects, and gain insights into the world of work, as he begins to form ambitions of his own. Even the clubs and societies open to him will become more advanced, as he becomes comfortable forming, presenting, and discussing complex ideas with older students and staff.
Alongside his intellectual development, he will have the opportunity to explore other passions through our broad and vibrant Co-curricular programme. In time, he will be given the chance to exercise leadership, collaborating with younger students in his House, leading them in Assemblies, and representing them in bodies such as Student Council. Indeed, this natural variance and diversity of opportunity is key to the open culture we foster at Whitgift, which helps students across the School gel with one another, and form valuable friendships, no matter when they joined.
George Sports Scholar
Taiko Drumming Workshop
Every year, Japanese Language students in the Third Form get the opportunity to engage in a Taiko Drumming workshop. This experience helps them enhance their appreciation for diverse cultures, fostering a global perspective, all while enjoying some fun beyond the classroom!
The Middle Years' Drama Production
Students have the chance to showcase their talents in the annual Middle Years' production. In 2023, the ensemble of Remote graced the stage for three nights, presenting a powerful performance that explored the profound struggles of a young individual dealing with feelings of despair, protest, and friendship.
Wellbeing
The Tutor and the Year group teams provide emotional support and guidance on a whole range of topics, nurturing each pupil in his quest to find his ‘happy place’ and thrive in his chosen field, be that academically, creatively, sportingly or socially.
Science
We are going to be facing an increasingly complex web of challenges at the nexus of science, technology and society over the next decade: gene editing, Artificial Intelligence, ubiquitous surveillance, advanced human enhancement, and a growing convergence between material, biological and cyber technologies, to name but a few. The teaching of Science at Whitgift builds understanding based on current knowledge but also constructs a platform to encourage creative development of ideas.
Sport
Basketball is one of 40 Sports to choose from. Basketball at Whitgift is all about discovering a passion and giving everyone the opportunity to be part of a team sport. Having fun and training hard has led to continuous improvement and all participating age groups are ranked in the top three teams in the LISBA League.
Trinity Term events
During the Trinity Term, both Third and Fifth Form students commemorate important milestones in their journey at Whitgift. Third Formers bid farewell to their blue shirts at the 'End of Blue Shirt' event, marking a symbolic transition. Simultaneously, Fifth Formers celebrate completing their GCSE examinations, marking a pivotal achievement in their academic journey.

The Welfare and Safeguarding Sub‑Committee provides strategic oversight to ensure the School meets its statutory safeguarding duties and maintains a safe, supportive environment for all pupils and staff.
Governor members are Andy Hulme (chair) and Mark Semmence.

Governor members are Asif Patel (chair), Elizabeth Clarke and Krishan Laladia.
These committees bring together the senior leadership and governors.

English Literature
AIMS
The English Literature department at Whitgift is committed to fostering a deep appreciation for the power of storytelling and literary exploration. The curriculum aims to develop a global perspective through the study of diverse texts, encouraging students to engage with different cultures, viewpoints, and ideas. In the Junior Years, pupils are introduced to a broad range of challenging and exciting literature, enhancing their critical thinking, writing, and communication skills. Through lively discussion, drama, and creative writing, students are encouraged to develop an enquiring enthusiasm for English that will stay with them for life.
The study of English Literature at Whitgift is designed not only to cultivate academic excellence but also to inspire a love for reading and writing, enabling pupils to interpret the world around them through the lens of literature. By engaging with both classic and contemporary works, students gain a nuanced understanding of human experiences and emotions, preparing them for further study and the wider world.
ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES
The English Literature department offers a variety of enrichment opportunities to extend learning beyond the classroom. Yearly residential trips to literary festivals and visits to Stratford-upon-Avon immerse students in the world of literature and drama, allowing them to experience the cultural and historical significance of the works they study. In addition, the School hosts its own Junior Literary Festival, where authors are invited to lead workshops and share their insights into the craft of writing.
Shakespeare plays a central role in the curriculum, with the annual Second Form Shakespeare evening offering students the opportunity to perform abridged versions of his works. Literary Societies tailored to each year group encourage further engagement with literature, while the Journalism, Play Writing, Play Reading, and Film Societies provide additional avenues for students to explore their creative and analytical skills. These activities help students connect with literature on a personal level, deepening their understanding and appreciation of the subject.

Biology
Aims
The Biology department at Whitgift is committed to nurturing a deep understanding of the life sciences, emphasising their pivotal role in addressing the global challenges that students will encounter in their future. Through a curriculum that spans from molecular biology to ecosystems, we aim to foster a genuine interest in the living world, cultivating students into biologically literate global citizens. Our approach ensures that pupils become well-versed in the principles of the scientific method, developing critical thinking skills that are essential for analysing and solving complex biological problems.
At Whitgift, Biology education goes beyond the classroom. We place a strong emphasis on building transferable skills, such as resilience and creativity, which empower students to approach the world with a problem-solving mindset. By engaging with real-world biological issues, students learn to apply scientific concepts in innovative ways, preparing them to make meaningful contributions to society.
Enrichment opportunities
The Whitgift Biomedical Science Diploma, available to Lower Sixth students, offers an in-depth exploration of biomedical sciences, providing a solid foundation for those interested in pursuing careers in healthcare and research. Field trips to Devon, designed for A Level students, offer hands-on field study experiences, where students can observe and analyse ecological systems in a natural setting. Additionally, our Animal Club and Horticultural Club allow students to engage with biology outside the classroom, fostering a deeper connection with the natural world and enhancing their understanding of biological processes. These opportunities are integral to our mission of developing well-rounded, scientifically literate individuals ready to tackle the challenges of the future.

Computer Science
AIMS
In an era increasingly defined by digital technology, the Computer Science department at Whitgift is committed to equipping students with the skills needed to thrive in a rapidly evolving job market. Our courses are designed to address the future of work, where many traditional roles may be automated or replaced by new technologies. Through a dynamic curriculum that covers a wide range of topics - including app development, database design, programming, website creation, game development, cybersecurity, and hardware - students gain valuable experience in both theoretical and practical aspects of computer science. The programme emphasises problem-solving and independence, encouraging students to navigate complex challenges and develop innovative solutions on their own.
ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES
To complement our core curriculum, the Computer Science department offers a variety of enrichment opportunities that allow students to deepen their understanding and apply their skills in exciting ways. Our new modules on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning introduce students to foundational concepts and practical applications of these technologies, including ethical considerations and real-world implications.
Students can also engage in national and international coding competitions such as the UK Bebras Computational Thinking Challenge, Informatics Olympiad, and Algorithmic Olympiad. These events provide a platform for students to showcase their problem-solving and coding skills, fostering a competitive spirit and recognizing their achievements.
Additionally, our Robotics Club gives students the chance to build and program robots, merging coding skills with mechanical engineering and teamwork. The Game Development Club allows students to design, code, and test their own video games, providing a creative outlet for their technical skills. Curriculum enhancements, such as modules on emerging technologies like blockchain, virtual reality (VR), and the Internet of Things (IoT), keep students at the forefront of technological advancements and prepare them for future trends. Through these varied opportunities, Whitgift’s Computer Science department ensures that students are not only adept in their technical skills but also well-prepared for the digital challenges of tomorrow.

Economics and Business
AIMS
The Economics and Business department at Whitgift offers a comprehensive and engaging curriculum designed to immerse students in the dynamic world of economics. The iGCSE Economics course provides an academically stimulating experience where students explore a wide range of relevant and current issues. In the first year, the focus is on fundamental concepts such as market competition, the effects of government intervention, and the principles of supply and demand. As students progress into the second year, they delve into more advanced topics, including interest rates, globalisation, and international trade. This structured approach ensures that students build a solid foundation in economic theory and its real-world applications. For those interested in extending their study, Economics can be pursued further at A Level in the Sixth Form.
ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES
To complement the rigorous academic curriculum, the Economics and Business department provides a range of enrichment opportunities that deepen students' understanding and application of economic concepts. The Whitonomics Magazine, a student-run publication, offers a platform for students to research, write, and discuss current economic issues, enhancing their analytical and communication skills.
The Economics Enrichment Society and the Investment Society are both integral to the department, providing students with additional avenues to explore their interests in economics and business. The Economics Enrichment Society hosts guest speakers, debates, and workshops that cover contemporary economic topics and trends, while the Investment Society allows students to engage with financial markets, investment strategies, and portfolio management, offering practical experience alongside their academic studies.
These enrichment activities not only support the classroom learning experience but also prepare students for future academic and professional pursuits in the field of economics and business. Through these opportunities, Whitgift ensures that students are well-equipped to understand and navigate the complexities of the modern economic landscape.

French
AIMS
At Whitgift, the French department is dedicated to igniting a passion for the French language among our students. Our mission is to foster a deep-seated interest in languages and a nuanced appreciation of cultural diversity, which will prepare students to thrive in an increasingly globalised society. Through a comprehensive and challenging curriculum, we emphasise the cognitive benefits of language learning and strive to enhance students' mastery of French while also deepening their understanding of English. We are particularly proud of our track record in motivating students to continue their language studies into the Sixth Form, with around 50% opting to study a language at this level and many pursuing higher education in languages.
ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES
To enrich the learning experience, the French department offers a range of dynamic opportunities that immerse students in French culture and language. One of the highlights is the annual exchange program to Toulouse, which provides students with an immersive experience in a French-speaking environment. This exchange helps students to practice their language skills and gain firsthand insights into French culture.
Additionally, our students can participate in the Joutes Oratoires, a national debating competition where they engage in rigorous debates, enhancing their language proficiency and public speaking skills. The department also organises work experience placements in France, allowing students to apply their language skills in real-world settings and gain valuable professional experience. A residential trip to Brussels further expands students' exposure to Francophone culture and institutions, while the French Ciné Club offers a platform for students to explore French cinema, deepening their cultural and linguistic understanding. These enriching activities complement the academic curriculum, providing students with a well-rounded education in French language and culture.

Classics
Aims
The Classics curriculum is designed to cultivate a deep comprehension of Latin and Greek languages, focusing on reading and interpreting texts. From the very beginning, students are immersed in the rich tapestry of Roman and Greek civilisations, learning not just the linguistic nuances but also the cultural, stylistic, and ethical dimensions that underpin these ancient societies. The course treats language as a gateway to literature and the cultural heritage of antiquity, rather than merely a tool for mental discipline or academic exercise. By engaging with the original texts, students gain invaluable insights into the literary works and the civilisations from which they originate.
Enrichment Opportunities
The Classics department offers a variety of enrichment opportunities that extend learning beyond the classroom. Biennial trips to historically significant sites in Italy, Greece, and Sicily allow students to experience the ancient world firsthand. Whether exploring the ruins of Pompeii, the temples of Athens, or the archaeological treasures of Sicily, these excursions bring the classical world to life, deepening students' understanding and appreciation of the subject.
In addition to travel opportunities, the department fosters a vibrant intellectual community through its Junior and Senior Classics Societies. These societies provide a platform for students of all levels to engage in discussions, presentations, and activities centered on classical themes, often led by both staff and students. Moreover, for those eager to expand their linguistic horizons, the department offers the unique chance to begin studying Ancient Greek in the Third Form, giving students an early start on mastering a new and challenging language.

German
AIMS
The German department at Whitgift is dedicated to cultivating a passion for the German language and an appreciation for German-speaking cultures. Our goal is to provide students with the skills and insights needed to navigate a globalised world effectively. We deliver a rigorous language curriculum designed to enhance cognitive abilities and deepen students' understanding of English, all while developing their fluency in German. Our approach not only fosters linguistic proficiency but also encourages students to engage critically with cultural contexts. We are especially proud of our efforts to inspire students to continue studying German into the Sixth Form, with around 50% choosing to study a language at this level and many pursuing advanced degrees in languages.
ENRICHMENT OPPORTUNITIES
To complement the academic curriculum, the German department offers a variety of enrichment activities that immerse students in the German language and culture. One notable opportunity is participation in the Oxford German Olympiad, a national competition that invites students to creatively express themselves in German through writing or filming. This competition provides a platform for students to showcase their language skills and creativity.
Additionally, our students have the chance to enter the prestigious Stephen Spender Translation Prize competition, where top linguists from each Key Stage compete in translating complex texts. This national competition, held in the Trinity term, challenges students to demonstrate their advanced language skills and analytical abilities.
Our long-standing exchange programmes further enhance students' cultural experiences. Second Form students have the opportunity to participate in an exchange with a school in Nuremberg, while Third Form students can engage in an exchange with a school in Munich. These exchanges, which have been successfully running for over 20 years, allow students to immerse themselves in German culture and practice their language skills in authentic settings. Through these enriching experiences, students gain a deeper connection to the language and culture, preparing them for future academic and professional pursuits.

Academic Drama
Academic Drama at Whitgift is a robust and academic subject that demands a great deal from those who study it. Drama students are independent learners who create their own original pieces of theatre, study diverse texts and how they might be realised in performance, as well as analysing and evaluating the work of other theatre makers, both of their peers and professionals.
At Whitgift, pupils have access to expert Drama teaching from the moment that they arrive. Drama is a key part of the curriculum, where core skills are imparted and cultivated, and nascent talents are fed and encouraged. Theatre is also used to explore different topics and themes, encouraging pupils to express their own views and feelings in a safe and balanced way.
Third Form pupils can choose to prepare for the prospect of Drama GCSE with a more rigorous offering. This year long course introduces pupils to a deeper analysis of performance texts through academic writing and in relation to theatre theory.
At Whitgift we follow the AQA specifications at both GCSE and A Level. Both courses encourage independent and confident learners to explore rich heritages of performance, as well as challenging themselves to develop as multi-disciplinary theatre makers and critics. Plays such as Blood Brothers and The Crucible are studied in-depth at GCSE, whereas A Level students work with a panoply of plays, old and new, including Our Country’s Good and Jerusalem. Study of live theatre is also an important part of GCSE and A Level practice, with frequent trips to world class productions taking place throughout the year.
